sources.citation: Blench, Roger. [n.d; captured 2024-07-24]. Miship opening page. rogerblench.info, West Chadic A3 section.
sources.note: One paragraph: 'Miship is a West Chadic language within the A3 cluster, apparently an isolate branch. Fieldwork was conducted in October 2019, which is currently being transcribed.' No documents posted; only reference Jungraithmayr 1965 [=1964]. Nothing on phonology.

sources.citation: Newman, Paul. 2022. A Chadic Bibliography, 5th ed. (items keyed 'Chip').
sources.note: Bibliography only. Chip-keyed items: Decker et al. 2021; Jungraithmayr 1964a; Kraft 1981; Mu'azu & Isah 2010a (ideophones), 2010b (grammar), 2010c (people/dialects), 2012 and 2016 (numerals). No phonology paper or thesis on Miship is listed.

sources.citation: Decker, Ken, Fittokka Gobak & Christina Riepe. 2021. A Sociolinguistic Profile of the Miship [mjs] Language of Plateau State, Nigeria. Journal of Language Survey Reports 2021-046. Dallas: SIL International. 49 pp.
sources.note: Most recent first-hand data (two-dialect wordlist, 49 pp.); SIL Plateau-State survey reports of this series carry a short phonology section (consonants, vowels, sometimes tone). Blocked here only by an automated-access block on sil.org and the Internet Archive outage; retry via web.archive.org id_ capture of the sil.org reapdata PDF.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2020. An Atlas of Nigerian Languages, 4th ed. Entry 320 'Miship'.
sources.note: Entry: Ship/Chip/Cip; Plateau State, Mangu and Shendam LGAs; 10,127 (Ames 1934), 6,000 (SIL); Chadic West A3; dialects Longmaar, Jibaam; Refs Wordlist: Jungraithmayr (1965), Grammar: Mu'azu & Katwal (2010). No phonology.

sources.citation: [LINCOM Europa]. 2010. Publisher's notice of Mu'azu & Isah, A grammar of the Miship language. California Linguistic Notes 35(2), 1 p.
sources.note: Blurb only: confirms the grammar has a sound-system chapter with consonants, vowels, 'other related phonological aspects' and 'the tonal system'. No stress statement.

sources.citation: Muazu [Mu'azu], Mohammed Aminu & Katwal Pemark Isah. 2010. The Miship: People, language, and dialects. California Linguistic Notes 35(2), Spring 2010, pp. 1-16.
sources.note: Sociolinguistic/dialect article (Longmaar vs Jibaam). Sec. 7.4 'Phonological differences between Longmaar and Jibaam dialects' (pp. 12-13) covers only /a/ ~ /e/ and initial /a/ deletion in question words. Nothing on stress, accent or tone ('accent' occurs once, p. 10, in the generic dialect-vs-accent definition).

sources.citation: Muazu, Mohammed Aminu & Katwal Pemark Isah. 2010. A descriptive analysis of Miship ideophones. California Linguistic Notes 35(2), Spring 2010, pp. 1-9.
sources.note: Ideophone typology and syllable structures (CVC, CVC-CVC, CVC-CVV, CVC-CVCVC, CVCVC-CVC); generic remark (p. 2) that ideophones show 'tonal patterns consisting either of all high tones or of all low tones'. No statement on word stress.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x langdoc listing for mish1244 (12 references).
sources.note: Only one grammar (Mu'azu & Isah 2010); the rest are wordlists, comparative works, ethnographic overviews and the 2021 SIL survey. No phonology-typed reference exists for Miship.
Sections on people, Bible translation, names, words, numerals; no phonology, no stress.

sources.locator: Abstract, p. 7; second sentence p. 20 (introducing the tone-marked Mupun/Miship word lists a-g, pp. 20-23)
sources.note: A sociolinguistic language-contact study, not a tone description. It asserts (abstract p. 7, body p. 20, conclusion p. 23) that Mupun and Miship have 'similar lexical items, tones and meanings' with only 'negligible variations in tones', and supports this with c. 60 Mupun/Miship word pairs from recorded speech transcribed with three tone diacritics (acute, macron, grave: e.g. Miship káap 'baboon', ās 'dog', pās 'arrow', kòp 'spear', túul 'pot', yèr 'bird', mát 'woman' vs Mupun màt), i.e. high/mid/low marking, but it states no tone inventory, tone-bearing unit or tonal process.
